title: He Scored 19,346 Runs and Led New Zealand to Their Finest Hour. Kane Williamson Has Retired.
excerpt: From Ahmedabad debut to WTC glory, the quiet genius from Tauranga leaves international cricket with tributes pouring in from Kohli, Gambhir, and the IPL family that adopted him
body:
Kane Williamson has announced his retirement from international cricket, ending a 16-year career that made him New Zealand's all-time leading run-scorer and one of the most universally respected batsmen of his generation.

The 35-year-old right-hander confirmed his decision on Friday, just days before the Black Caps' second Test against England at The Oval. He departs with 9,515 Test runs at an average of 54.06, 6,554 ODI runs at 47.48, and 3,277 T20I runs — a combined 19,346 international runs with 48 centuries across formats.

"I've always felt a strong drive and hunger for international cricket, and I take pride in knowing I've given it my all in every match I've played for New Zealand," Williamson said. "Continuing with anything less wouldn't be right, and I feel fortunate to step away on my own terms."

## A Captain Who Changed New Zealand Cricket

Williamson captained New Zealand across all three formats between 2016 and 2024, leading the Black Caps to the inaugural World Test Championship title in 2021 — a victory against India in Southampton that remains one of the defining moments of modern cricket. He also steered the side to successive ODI World Cup finals in 2015 and 2019, the latter ending in one of the most dramatic finishes in cricket history: a super-over loss to England at Lord's.

His ICC accolades include Cricketer of the Year in 2015, Test Player of the Year in 2019, and a record four Sir Richard Hadlee Medals for New Zealand's best cricketer. He made his debut as a 20-year-old against India in Ahmedabad in November 2010, and his final international appearance came at Lord's last week, where he scored 0 and 18 on a pitch the ICC later rated unsatisfactory.

## India's Farewell to 'Kano'

The tributes from the Indian cricket fraternity have been swift and deeply personal — a reflection of how embedded Williamson became in Indian cricket culture through his years in the IPL. He spent eight seasons with Sunrisers Hyderabad from 2015 to 2022, scoring 2,101 runs in 76 matches and finishing as the leading run-scorer in IPL 2018 with 735 runs. He captained SRH to the 2018 final and later joined Gujarat Titans.

Virat Kohli posted a tribute on X calling Williamson a friend beyond cricket: "From an opponent to a friend over the years. It's been a pleasure watching you bat and compete against you over so many years, but more than that I value our friendship and shared perspectives on the game and beyond."

India head coach Gautam Gambhir was characteristically succinct: "Grace + Talent + Spirit = Kane Williamson."

Rashid Khan, Williamson's former SRH teammate, called him "one of the calmest minds, finest players, and greatest gentlemen our game has ever seen. Kane Mama, it was an honour to share a dressing room and the field with you." David Warner, who alternated the SRH captaincy with Williamson, posted a photo collage from their IPL days with the caption "THE SRH BOYS…!!!!"

## Why the Diaspora Will Remember Him

For Indian cricket fans in the US, UK, and Canada — many of whom followed Williamson through years of late-night IPL streaming — his retirement closes a chapter in a rivalry that was defined by mutual admiration rather than animosity. Williamson, along with Kohli, Joe Root, and Steve Smith, formed cricket's so-called Fab Four, a quartet of batting peers whose careers overlapped and intertwined across a golden era of Test cricket.

His best Test knock against India — a resolute 89 in Wellington in 2020, during a series India was favoured to win — encapsulated the Williamson method: patience, precision, and an almost preternatural ability to find gaps without apparent effort. That the WTC final he won as captain came against India only deepened his connection with Indian fans, who respected the quality even as they mourned the result.

Williamson will continue playing franchise cricket. He is currently contracted with Middlesex in the T20 Blast and remains eligible for future IPL seasons. But the international stage, where he scored 19,346 runs across 378 matches, has seen its last of the quiet genius from Tauranga.

New Zealand coach Rob Walter summed it up: "Anyone who's had the privilege of working with Kane understands he is a very special player and person. He's an incredible player, awesome teammate, a wonderful leader and a fantastic ambassador for our sport."

*Sources: Reuters, Cricket.com.au, ICC Cricket, NewKerala*
